prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 , the provision for credit losses was $2.8 million and $8.1 million, respectively, compared to $2.5 million and $9.0 million for the same respective periods last year. The increase in the provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to an increase in the reserve for unfunded commitments. The decrease in the provision for credit losses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to a $1.6 million recovery of a commercial mortgage loan in the first quarter of 2026.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Table 4 presents the components of noninterest expense.

Total salaries and benefits expense decreased by $0.6 million or 1% in the third quarter of 2026, primarily due to decreases in separation expense, share-based compensation expense, and incentive compensation, partially offset by an increase in medical, dental, and life insurance expense which was driven by higher costs incurred in connection with medical insurance. Total salaries and benefits expense increased by $6.3 million or 3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period last year, primarily due to increases in base salaries primarily due to annual merit increases, medical, dental, and life insurance expense, and share-based compensation related to the accelerated vesting during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 of restricted stock awards pursuant to the retirement provisions of performance-based restricted stock awards granted in 2024 and 2025.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text:
Table 5 presents our provision for income taxes and effective tax rates.

The provision for income taxes was $19.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $5.0 million compared to the same period last year. The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 23.2%, an increase from 21.3% for the same period last year. The higher effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year was primarily due to a decrease in tax exempt income and a decrease in tax benefits from discrete items.

The provision for income taxes was $54.8 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $15.4 million compared to the same period last year. The effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 22.8%, an increase from 21.4% for the same period last year. The higher effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period last year was primarily due to higher pretax book income, which reduced the benefit of tax advantaged investments, as well as an increase in non-deductible compensation and a decrease in tax benefits from discrete items.

net.text: Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $64.3 million, an increase of $10.9 million, or 20.5%, compared to the same period in 2025. Diluted earnings per common share was $1.49 for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $0.29, or 24.2%, compared to the same period in 2025.

da.text: Net equipment expense increased by $1.0 million or 10% in the third quarter of 2026 and by $2.1 million or 7% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods last year, primarily due to higher depreciation expense and software license fees and maintenance.

sbc.text: Total salaries and benefits expense decreased by $0.6 million or 1% in the third quarter of 2026, primarily due to decreases in separation expense, share-based compensation expense, and incentive compensation, partially offset by an increase in medical, dental, and life insurance expense which was driven by higher costs incurred in connection with medical insurance. Total salaries and benefits expense increased by $6.3 million or 3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period last year, primarily due to increases in base salaries primarily due to annual merit increases, medical, dental, and life insurance expense, and share-based compensation related to the accelerated vesting during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 of restricted stock awards pursuant to the retirement provisions of performance-based restricted stock awards granted in 2024 and 2025. Medical, dental, and life insurance expense increased by $2.4 million or 20% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period last year, primarily due to higher costs incurred in connection with medical insurance.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text: Net interest income is affected by the size and mix of our balance sheet components as well as the spread between interest earned on assets and interest paid on liabilities. Net interest margin is defined as net interest income, on a taxable-equivalent basis, as a percentage of average earning assets.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Table 3 presents the components of noninterest income.

Trust and asset management income is comprised of fees earned from the management and administration of trusts and other customer assets. The management fees are largely based upon the market value of the assets and the fee rate charged to customers. Total trust assets under administration were $14.2 billion and $12.6 billion as of September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively. Trust and asset management income increased by $0.8 million or 7% in the third quarter of 2026 and by $3.1 million or 9% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods last year, primarily due to the increase in trust assets under management.

Fees, exchange, and other service charges decreased by $4.4 million or 29% in the third quarter of 2026 and by $11.1 million or 25% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods last year, primarily due to lower merchant income following the sale of our merchant services portfolio in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Annuity and insurance income increased by $1.0 million or 93% in the third quarter of 2026 and by $1.5 million or 37% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods last year, primarily due to higher production resulting from expanded product offerings and improved referral activity during the three and nine…

intro.text: Bank of Hawaii Corporation (“Bank of Hawai‘i Corporation” or the “Parent”) is a Delaware corporation and a bank holding company (“BHC”) headquartered in Honolulu, Hawai‘i. The Parent’s principal operating wholly-owned subsidiary, Bank of Hawai‘i (“Bank of Hawaiʻi” or the “Bank”), was organized on December 17, 1897, and is chartered by the State of Hawai‘i. The Bank’s deposits are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the “FDIC”) and the Bank is a member of the Federal Reserve System. The Bank, directly and through its subsidiaries, provides a broad range of financial products and services primarily to customers in Hawaiʻi, Guam, and other Pacific Islands. References to “we,” “our,” “us,” or “the Company” refer to the Parent and its subsidiaries and are consolidated for financial reporting purposes.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
